## Runs 6–7 — spot-check read before the Landau fan

Raw signed Rxx and drain-current traces precede the FFT/onset plots below (`sdh-spot-check`; only sr1, B_1–B_2, is connected). Both runs completed without clipping: electron run 6 at n=+3.2 reaches 530 Ohm, hole run 7 at n=-1.2 reaches 587 Ohm; drain current remains 9.81–9.94 nA. Negative excursions are retained, not rectified or log-clipped. Only positive B is available: Hall admixture and lack of even-in-B symmetrization remain limitations.

Run 6 has candidate content around 7, 15, 22 and 29 T; run 7 around 5–7 and 12–13 T. These are **candidate frequencies, not independent pocket counts**: the electron comb needs density tracking and a Luttinger-aware harmonic screen, and extraction of the slow component varies with the fit window. The global 0.3–10 T onset fit reports a censored 0.3 T edge, but its low-B residual is dominated by the background fit through the large 8–10 T MR feature; moreover the 50 mT grid below 1 T fails the full-density Nyquist test. Restricting the background fit to 0.3–5 T/degree 5 gives a non-censored headline onset of 1.018 T for the 6.8 T component. That component has the same onset with degree 3 (0.3–4 T/degree 5: 1.03 T; 0.3–6 T/degree 5: 1.01 T), although the full tone search can promote a near-residual 3.1–3.2 T component to the headline under those other fits. The chosen onset is therefore a local, component-supported estimate; low-frequency onset ambiguity remains. This local fit supplies the fan onset; the high-field global result remains a documented extraction failure mode, not evidence of low-field SdH. No absence claim is made below 1 T.

**Decision:** acquire one electron-side, D≈0 fan in the high-density part of the accessible window, including n=+3.2 for direct acquisition comparison with run 6. The hole side is gate-limited to about -1.27 and lies in the near-CNP model ambiguity. Classification remains **uninformative** until cross-density trajectories and both ABAB/adjacent-N overlays have been checked. The calibration is ridge A from run 5; its second ridge is a possible density-inhomogeneity confound, not established mixed stacking. Absolute density retains the geometry-scale uncertainty.

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, plot_raw, sdh_onset, sdh_fft
out=Path('hera_scratch')
for rid,n in [(6,3.2),(7,-1.2)]:
 r=open_run(f'data/{rid}')
 fig=plot_raw(r); fig.savefig(out/f'spot_{rid}_raw.png',dpi=140); plt.show()
 ch={c.cid:c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
 B=r.col('magnet_field'); I=r.col('sr0_X')/ch['sr0'].gain; R=r.col('sr1_X')/ch['sr1'].gain/I
 print(f'Run {rid}: n={n}, signed R {R.min():.2f}..{R.max():.2f} Ohm; I {I.min()*1e9:.3f}..{I.max()*1e9:.3f} nA')
 on=sdh_onset(R,B,r_full_scale=5000); print(on.summary())
 fig,axs=plt.subplots(2,2,figsize=(12,8))
 for deg in (3,5,7):
  sel=B>=0.3
  bg=np.polynomial.Polynomial.fit(B[sel],R[sel],deg)(B[sel])
  axs[0,0].plot(B[sel],R[sel]-bg,label=f'degree {deg}')
  for ax,lo in zip((axs[0,1],axs[1,0]),(1,2)):
   f,a=sdh_fft(R[:,None],B,b_range=(lo,8),bg_degree=deg,nfft=4096,log=False)
   ax.plot(f,a[0]/a[0].max(),label=f'deg {deg} B={lo}..8')
   p,_=find_peaks(a[0]); p=p[(f[p]>3)&(f[p]<50)]; p=p[np.argsort(a[0,p])[-6:]][::-1]
   print('FFT',rid,lo,deg,list(np.round(f[p],2)))
   ax.set_xlim(0,50); ax.axvline(abs(n)*10.33916924,color='k',ls='--'); ax.set_xlabel('F (T)'); ax.legend()
 for t in on.tones: axs[1,1].plot(t.b_centers,t.snr,label=f'{t.freq:.1f} T')
 axs[1,1].set_yscale('log');axs[1,1].axhline(5,color='k'); axs[1,1].legend(fontsize=7);axs[1,1].set_xlabel('B (T)');axs[1,1].set_ylabel('matched filter SNR')
 axs[0,0].set_xlabel('B (T)');axs[0,0].set_ylabel('signed residual R (Ohm)');axs[0,0].legend()
 fig.suptitle(f'Run {rid}, sr1 B_1-B_2; positive field only, no B symmetrization available');fig.tight_layout();fig.savefig(out/f'spot_{rid}_fft.png',dpi=140);plt.show()
r=open_run('data/6');ch={c.cid:c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
B=r.col('magnet_field');R=r.col('sr1_X')/ch['sr1'].gain/(r.col('sr0_X')/ch['sr0'].gain)
print('Local onset audit: restrict the background fit below the large high-field MR feature')
for hi,deg in [(4,5),(5,3),(5,5),(6,5)]:
 on=sdh_onset(R,B,b_hi=hi,bg_degree=deg,r_full_scale=5000)
 print(f'B_hi={hi}, degree={deg}: '+on.summary())

## HERA — electron-side D≈0 Landau fan for the stacking read

> **05:25** · D=0 electron fan: n=2.8..3.2e12, B=1.0176..6.4690 T, 228x11, 3 s dwell, Si=0, base T, sr1 50 uV · **ETA ~09:10** (≈3h45m)

`landau-fan-vti` (base `landau-fan`), in-arc Step 4 of `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count`. Gates A/B remain satisfied in the operator's unchanged kernel (measure 18 executed [10], VERIFY 32 [17], handoff 44 [23], BOUND 46 [24]); Gate C passed in runs 0–3. Runs 6–7 and their raw/FFT/onset audit are in ana 14–15. Choose the electron side: it accesses the separated high-density templates, while the hole-side limit n≈−1.27 lies in the near-CNP ambiguity. Only sr1 (B_1–B_2) supplies a regional read; sr2/sr3 are unconnected. The second CNP ridge in run 5 remains a density-inhomogeneity confound.

**Design and claim window.** n=+2.8…+3.2×10¹² cm⁻², D=0 under ridge-A calibration (run 5, same rounded constants as run 6; ratio calibrated, absolute scale a geometry prior). TG=0.869016…0.983621 V and BG=1.017844…1.166125 V; Si remains 0 V. `sdh_onset` on the run-6 0.3–5 T local background fit gives B_lo=1.017618 T, carried by the 6.8 T component. Its per-tone onset is 1.01–1.03 T across neighboring fits; the global fit falsely revives low-field background and remains a documented extraction ambiguity (ana 15). The forward model `fs_count_b0.abab_fs` gives [6.038,22.914] T at n=2.8 and [7.306,25.783] T at n=3.2, versus ABCA F_L=[28.950,33.085] T. B_hi=6.468987 T is the five-period floor for the smallest nominal partner: Δ(1/B)=0.828103 T⁻¹, δF=1.208 T, 2δF=2.415 T below the ≥6.038 T heavy/singleton separation. Per-tone usable reach and any fitted density rescale will be re-audited after acquisition; these nominal numbers do not guarantee a resolved partner.

**Both-axis sampling and cost floor.** 228 B rows uniform in 1/B, step 0.00364803 T⁻¹; 11 density points, step 0.040×10¹² cm⁻². The n-ray floor at B_lo is 0.0492×10¹² for two samples per period, or 0.0410 allowing a 20% scale increase; 11 is the minimum over this window. F_L at n_max is 33.09 T (≤45.0 T allowing the second-ridge offset and +20% scale), but run 6's high-B candidate content extends to roughly 130 T. To keep that content from folding into the pocket band, the B grid uses a 136.5 T Nyquist design bound (5% frequency margin): 228 is the minimum. This exceeds the recipe's usual ≤200-row coarse start because its binding sampling floor takes precedence. Higher-order n-ray shapes are not a claim of this density grid. A coarser B grid is not being used to save time.

**Acquisition/headroom.** Keep τ=0.3 s and 24 dB/oct on sr0/sr1; 3 s dwell=10τ, matching the spot checks' blocking-magnet settle floor. Keep sr1 at 50 µV (5 kΩ full scale at 10 nA), sr0 at 20 mV. Run 6's full 0–10 T peak is 530 Ω; scaling by 3.2/2.8 and a further factor 3 for the lower-density corner gives a conservative 1.82 kΩ design allowance, below 37% FS. This is an estimate, not a measured corner; the 90%-FS guard stops before clipping. All followed channels, phases, temperatures and both gate currents are plotted live and recorded.

**Price and coverage trade.** From the measured handoff field near zero, positioning to B_lo costs 7.43 min and the sweep traverse costs 39.80 min at 1/7.3 T/min; total ramp floor 47.22 min, monotonically upward with no return traverse. Run 5 measured median point time 1.098 s at 1 s dwell (NPLC=1); use 3.2 s/point here including added vaporizer read, plus 6.1 s/row for the measured ~3.08 s field overhead (runs 6–7), slow delay and gate flyback. 2,508 points ×3.2 s=133.8 min; ramp+rows gives 204.2 min, with 10% contingency ≈225 min. This narrow high-density fan excludes the hole side, CNP, and low electrons: those add cost while weakening the immediate model separation. Covering the full accessible −1.27…+3.27 window at the same steps would take roughly 25 h including contingency and still would not resolve the vanishing low-electron partner. The limited density span may leave ABAB versus adjacent-N trajectories inconclusive; no broad-density or whole-flake verdict is promised.

**Preflight and checkpoints.** Before any write, compare actual base temperatures, advancing logfiles, heaters off, field/gates at the handoff state, Si range/output, exact card validators, drive, filter settings and gate pacing. Stop on mismatch. Inspect the first three rows for leakage, clipping, flat/dead channels and current stability; then inspect every 30 min and when crossing 3 T and 5 T. Existing 1 nA gate-current trip, base-T/freshness and headroom checks run during acquisition. At each checkpoint continue only if quality holds; if the shared n=3.2 column fails to reproduce run 6, withhold classification and stop for review. Early partial inverse-field records cannot establish tone absence. Completion: raw native-grid map first, then per-column signed-R FFT stability/harmonic audit, shared-density comparison, whole-set scale/Luttinger fit and ABAB plus adjacent-N overlays. Leave B and gates at their final actual values pending analysis. On the VTI, a notebook interrupt does **not** halt an in-progress supply ramp; operator action is needed for that (rig card). Pointwise guards act after the blocking field move finishes.
